samples.summary: The disposal revocation of `getStore().setPageSetup` — the one member the guard proxy never forwards — has no test
samples.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` was deliberately rerouted from `docStore` to `revocableStore` and the comment calls this "the single page-setup-shaped hole left in a disposed handle". The new suite `a disposed editor is inert` (packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:~1030-1090) exercises `getStore().insertText`, `deleteBlock` and `getDoc().insertText`, but never `setPageSetup` through a handle after `dispose()`. Grepping editor-read-only.test.ts for `setPageSetup` returns nothing, and editor-page-setup.test.ts only calls `editor.setPageSetup(...)` on live editors (it calls `dispose()` solely in cleanup). So a regression that reverted this line to `docStore.setPageSetup` (or a `pageSetupGuardedStore` built over the raw store) would let a stale holder mutate the shared document's page geometry after revocation, with every test still green.

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore`'s non-`get` traps in the revoked state are untested, while the `readOnlyDocStore` twin has a full escape-hatch suite
samples.evidence: read-only.ts adds eight traps to `revocableDocStore` that switch on `isRevoked()` (`set`, `defineProperty`, `deleteProperty`, `getPrototypeOf`→null, `setPrototypeOf`, `preventExtensions`, `has`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`, `ownKeys`). The corresponding readOnly behaviour is pinned by dedicated tests (editor-read-only.test.ts:776 'the prototype is not a way around it', :816 'a prototype cannot be planted…', :839 'the handle cannot make the underlying store non-extensible', :852 '`in` reports what get will actually return', :795 'the live internal state is not reachable as a property'). The new `a disposed editor is inert` suite has no counterpart for any of them: it only exercises the `get` trap by calling neutered mutators. There is no unit test file for read-only.ts at all (grep for `revocableDocStore` matches only the source and editor.ts). A regression in, say, `getPrototypeOf` would leave a disposed handle escapable back to the live store.

samples.summary: The new disposed-editor guard in `insertImageFromUrl` has no test (only the `insertImageFromFile` twin got one)
samples.evidence: image-insert.ts adds an `editor.isDisposed()` early-return plus a toast in `insertImageFromUrl` (returning `false`). image-insert.test.ts adds only 'inserts nothing when the editor was disposed under the upload' for `insertImageFromFile`; the file imports `insertImageFromFile` and `shareTokenImageUploader` and never `insertImageFromUrl` (grep for `insertImageFromUrl` matches image-insert.ts and docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx only). The URL path's preflight `loadImageDimensions` is also a network round trip, so the same stale-write hazard applies with no coverage, and the `false` return value (which the toolbar branches on) is unasserted.

samples.summary: `SharedDocumentByToken`'s useState/useEffect → useQuery rewrite has no component-level test; only the extracted pure predicates are covered
samples.evidence: The component was rewritten to a `useQuery` with `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `retry: shouldRetryShareLinkResolve`, `enabled: Boolean(token)`, plus new branching (`token && isLoading`, `!token || fatal || !resolved`, message selection). share-links.test.ts covers only `isRevokedShareLinkError` / `isShareLinkResolveFatal` / `shouldRetryShareLinkResolve` as pure functions. Nothing asserts that the component wires them up: that a transient refetch failure keeps rendering the editor with the last good `resolved`, that a 404 on re-resolve closes the view, that a downgraded `role` actually propagates to `readOnly`, or that a missing token still shows 'No share token provided'. Glob for shared-document tests under packages/frontend found only shared-blob-routing.test.ts and shared-header-status.test.tsx. A miswired `enabled`/`fatal` expression would ship undetected even though the predicates pass.

samples.summary: The parameterized `${op} over a multi-block selection is one undo unit` tests assert only batch bookkeeping, so they pass even if the op writes nothing
samples.evidence: The loop over `['indent','outdent','toggleList']` asserts `watch.outermost() === 1` and `watch.writesOutsideABatch() === 0` and nothing else. Both hold trivially for an op whose `forEachBlockInSelection` body writes zero blocks (e.g. a selection that failed to register, or a guard that early-returns for every block) — `doc.batch()` is still called once and no write escapes. Only `indent` gets a separate effect assertion ('indent really moves every selected block'); `outdent` and `toggleList` have no round-trip or state assertion, so a regression that silently stops writing in those two arms would still be green.

samples.summary: `withUndoUnit`'s documented throw behaviour (held renders replayed once, even after the body throws) is untested
samples.evidence: `withUndoUnit`'s doc comment claims interior `requestRender()` calls are 'held and replayed once — at most once — after the outermost unit commits, including after a throw'. The only render-deferral coverage is the frontend 'paints once for the whole action, after the unit commits' test (editor-undo-selection.test.ts), which drives a successful typing action. Nothing drives a body that throws, so a regression that left `renderAfterUndoUnit` set (screen stuck showing the pre-throw state) or `undoUnitDepth` unbalanced would not be caught. Similarly, `MemDocStore.willWrite()` being called *before* each mutation — documented so a partially-applied throwing mutator stays undoable — has no test in the new memory.test.ts cases.
searchedFor: read packages/docs/test/store/memory.test.ts new cases in diff

samples.summary: Pre-existing test title 'should clear redo stack on new snapshot' now misdescribes the behaviour this diff introduced
samples.evidence: After the change, `snapshot()` no longer clears redo — `willWrite()` (the first write) does. The test still passes only because it follows the snapshot with `insertBlock`. It is no longer evidence for what its name claims, and the new 'snapshot() then a batch that writes nothing leaves redo intact' case asserts the opposite rule. Renaming it would keep the suite honest about which call clears redo.

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore`'s stated live-mode contract (stable member identity, `this` bound to the real store) has no test
samples.evidence: The doc comment states 'a member's identity is stable (`s.canUndo === s.canUndo`)' as a deliberate contract mirroring `pageSetupGuardedStore`. No test asserts it for the revocable wrapper; the new disposed-editor tests only call members. A regression dropping the memoization would break callers using a member as a dependency or map key, silently.

finding.summary: The disposal revocation of `getStore().setPageSetup` — the one member the guard proxy never forwards — has no test
finding.evidence: `guardedSetPageSetup` was deliberately rerouted from `docStore` to `revocableStore` and the comment calls this "the single page-setup-shaped hole left in a disposed handle". The new suite `a disposed editor is inert` (packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts:~1030-1090) exercises `getStore().insertText`, `deleteBlock` and `getDoc().insertText`, but never `setPageSetup` through a handle after `dispose()`. Grepping editor-read-only.test.ts for `setPageSetup` returns nothing, and editor-page-setup.test.ts only calls `editor.setPageSetup(...)` on live editors (it calls `dispose()` solely in cleanup). So a regression that reverted this line to `docStore.setPageSetup` (or a `pageSetupGuardedStore` built over the raw store) would let a stale holder mutate the shared document's page geometry after revocation, with every test still green.

verdict.reason: The claimed gap is real. `guardedSetPageSetup` routes through `revocableStore` (editor.ts:3307-3322) and the `get` trap returns it unconditionally (editor.ts:3325), making that line the sole enforcement of disposal revocation for `setPageSetup`. Repo-wide grep for `setPageSetup` yields only editor-page-setup.test.ts (live editors only; `dispose()` appears at 305/326/354 purely as trailing cleanup, with no post-dispose assertion), store/memory.test.ts, model/types.test.ts, docx-exporter.test.ts, plus frontend tests that mock `editor.setPageSetup` or drive YorkieDocStore directly. The new `a disposed editor is inert` suite (editor-read-only.test.ts:957-1117), which I read in full, covers insertText/deleteBlock/getDoc writes/stale handles/paste/isDisposed but never `setPageSetup`, and contains no loop over store members (`for (const`/`forEach`/`each(` — no matches in that file). No test references `revocableDocStore` anywhere. So reverting line 3321 to `docStore.setPageSetup` would let a stale post-dispose holder persist page geometry into the shared document with all tests green — a missing test over a new guard-revocation behavior with data-affecting impact, blocking under this lens.
